evals.name: rising-cpa-after-scaling
evals.prompt: Meta sales campaign, Advantage+ campaign budget, 4 ad sets (3 interest stacks + 1 lookalike 1%), daily budget raised from €300 to €700 on Monday. Last 7 days vs previous 7: CPA €48 → €81, CPM €9.10 → €12.40, link CTR 1.4% → 0.9%, frequency 2.1 → 3.6, two ad sets show 'Learning limited'. Attribution 7-day click/1-day view, CAPI on, EMQ 7.2. Top ad has run since March 3rd. What's going on and what do I change?
evals.expected_output: Audit in the skill's format: identifies the >100% budget jump as a learning reset, creative fatigue (frequency, CTR drop, old creative), over-segmentation causing learning limited; recommends consolidating ad sets, new creative, stepping budget back and scaling ≤20%/day, with implementation order.
assertions: Attributes the CPA rise to the 133% budget increase resetting learning plus creative fatigue, citing frequency 3.6 and the CTR drop
Recommends consolidating the four ad sets (learning limited) into fewer, broader ad sets
Recommends new creative given the top ad has run since March and frequency is high
Scaling guidance is ≤20% per day and changes are batched to reset learning once
Attribution setting is named when quoting results and data trust is confirmed (CAPI on, EMQ 7.2)

evals.name: conversions-dropped-tracking-first
evals.prompt: Our Meta lead ads campaign showed 140 leads last month and 60 this month with the same spend. Nothing changed in the ads. Two weeks ago our agency installed a new cookie banner and switched attribution to 1-day click. Shopify shows about the same number of actual form submissions as last month. Should I pause the campaign?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the drop is most likely a reporting artefact (consent banner reducing browser events, attribution window change) since actual submissions are flat; recommends checking CAPI/consent and comparing with the same attribution setting before any campaign change; advises against pausing.
assertions: Identifies the attribution change and the new consent banner as the probable causes and notes actual submissions are flat
Advises not to pause or restructure the campaign on this evidence
Recommends verifying Conversions API, consent handling and comparing periods with the same attribution setting
Points to gtm-debugging-style verification steps for the tracking layer

evals.name: advantage-plus-vs-manual-decision
evals.prompt: E-commerce brand, $60k/month on Meta, ~90 purchases/week, 12 live creatives refreshed every two weeks, all in a manual sales campaign with broad targeting, highest volume bidding. ROAS 2.8 against a 2.5 target. Should we move to an Advantage+ sales campaign and should we use a cost per result goal?
evals.expected_output: Recommends testing an Advantage+ sales campaign given volume and creative pipeline, with an existing-customer budget cap, keeping highest volume initially and only adding a cost-per-result or ROAS goal set near achieved performance after the test stabilizes; describes the test design and what to compare.
assertions: Recommends an Advantage+ sales test and gives the reasons (volume ≥50/week, creative supply)
Mentions the existing-customer budget share/cap to protect prospecting
Advises keeping highest volume during learning and setting any cost or ROAS goal near achieved results, not aspirational
Describes how to compare manual vs Advantage+ (same creative, enough time, same attribution)
